analysis.title: Marketcolour + Mutual Fund / HF Update / Europe HC / VAR (dg) / Schindler / FLSmidth / Rational
key_insights: US equities fell for a 6th consecutive session (about 6% over the stretch). SPX -202bps to 7175 with 11/11 sectors down and VIX +16% to 28.47. NDX -221bps to 26517 (up 5% YTD). RTY -218bps to 2655.
The AI trade reversed lower after early strength. GS AI Semis basket (GSBSMHX) -2.91% and GS Data Center basket (GSTMTDAT) -2.29%. Consumer Discretionary -3.03% and Communication Services -2.92%.

Industrials is the second most net sold US sector MTD behind Info Tech, where net exposure is at its lowest level in more than two years. Consumer Staples is also among the most net sold sectors MTD, which GS reads as managers fading the sector's price rally.

Asset managers and HFs net sold macro products and net bought pockets of consumer and financials. No sector screened materially for sale. Liquidity is poor and exacerbating price action, with S&P top of book averaging $4mm on the touch.

42% of large-cap mutual funds are outperforming benchmarks YTD vs a historical average of 37%. Funds were underweight AI-exposed equities before the recent AI-complex weakness, at 722 bp underweight the Mag 7 at end of Q3 2026, effectively unchanged on the quarter.

Large-cap mutual funds are most overweight Industrials (+200 bp), Health Care (+199 bp, a 10-year high) and Financials (+196 bp). High return dispersion and better market breadth have supported fund returns.
Global fundamental L/S managers are -0.2% in November and +8.9% YTD as of Nov 16. November losses came from beta, partly offset by positive alpha from short-side gains.

Hedge funds heavily net sold global equities in November, with long and short sales at about 3 to 1. Single stocks were net sold in 7 of the last 8 weeks. Fundamental L/S net leverage fell another 7.6 pts MTD to its lowest in more than five years, below Liberation Day lows.
CTA desk: broader market weakness may be driven by systematic flow while liquidity is low. Weakness worsened at the US open and erased early gains in many names.

Europe healthcare: GS reiterates Buy on AstraZeneca, Bayer, Argenx (on conviction list), Galderma and UCB. Novartis stays Sell on patent expirations weighing on earnings momentum, with the stock at a premium to the sector.

Var Energy cut to Neutral. The 12m price target falls to NOK51 from NOK70 on new gas assumptions, leaving about 7% upside. GS cites longer-term downside risk to TTF gas prices, with upside risk to TTF this winter.

Schindler is Sell with a CHF250 target (15% downside). The market took the lack of precise quantitative margin guidance and no increase in shareholder cash distribution cautiously. The stock is up 20% over the last 3 months vs the sector down 2%.
FLSmidth: the author reiterates Buy as a contrarian stance. Feedback after the capital markets day targets and CFO change has been cautious, which is arguably reflected in a 20% fall in the stock.

Rational is Buy with a EUR833 target (35% upside). GS sees limited mid-term direct monetization and no new changes to the financial outlook from the capital markets day, but sees the moat vs peers and customer benefits strengthening.

market_movers.rationale: GS cites best-in-class growth and pipeline optionality, with valuation looking increasingly attractive.
Bayer: GS sees an underappreciated Pharma business and asymmetric risk reward.
Argenx is on the conviction list. GS cites outsized revenue growth supporting premium valuations.
Galderma: outsized revenue growth expected to support premium valuations.
UCB: outsized revenue growth expected to support premium valuations.
Patent expirations should keep weighing on earnings momentum, and the downside is not adequately reflected with the stock at a premium to the sector.
Var Energy: new gas assumptions cut the target from NOK70, citing longer-term downside risk to TTF prices.
Schindler: no precise quantitative margin guidance, consensus margins already near best-in-class, and no increase in shareholder cash distribution.
FLSmidth: contrarian Buy after a 20% fall following cautious post-CMD feedback.
Rational: the CMD strengthens its moat vs peers and improves customer benefits, though direct mid-term monetization is limited.
